assumptions: The scale is the published one named, applied over the window and normalisation stated.
limits: A scale is a propensity, not a structural prediction.
Different scales are not comparable, which is why the scale is named in the answer.
bio.jane/contract.question: How does a chosen physicochemical scale vary along this protein?

description: Windowed physicochemical profile along a protein (ExPASy ProtScale). Pass `scaleId` for any of the 57 scales ProtScale publishes plus the 14 Biopython tables it does not, with optional 0-1 normalisation; or pass `kind` for the five ProtParam profiles (hydropathy over the 28 GRAVY scales, Vihinen flexibility, Hopp & Woods hydrophilicity, Emini surface accessibility, Janin interior-to-surface transfer). Returns one value per window with the residue it centres on.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

edge.description: ProtScale relative weight of the window's edge residues, 0-1 (default 1 = unweighted).

kind.description: which profile to compute. Ignore this and pass `scaleId` to reach the full ProtScale catalogue.

normalize.description: ProtScale's 'normalize the scale from 0 to 1' — rescales the twenty scale values before windowing, so profiles from different scales are comparable. Requires `scaleId`.

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

scale.description: hydropathy scale. Values: KyteDoolitle (Kyte & Doolittle (1982)), Aboderin (Aboderin (Int J Biochem 2:537)), AbrahamLeo (Abraham & Leo (1987)), Argos (Argos (Eur J Biochem 128:565)), BlackMould (Black & Mould (1991)), BullBreese (Bull & Breese (1974)), Casari (Casari & Sippl, hydrophobic potential (JMB 224:725)), Cid (Cid (Protein Eng 5:373)), Cowan3.4 (Cowan at pH 3.4 (1990)), Cowan7.5 (Cowan at pH 7.5 (1990)), Eisenberg (Eisenberg, normalized consensus (1984)), Engelman (Engelman, transfer free energy (Annu Rev Biophys 15:321)), Fasman (Fasman (1989)), Fauchere (Fauchere (1983)), GoldSack (Goldsack & Chalifoux, free energy of mixing (J Theor Biol 39:645)), Guy (Guy, transfer free energy kcal/mol (1985)), Jones (Jones (J Theor Biol 50:167)), Juretic (Juretic (Theor Comput Chem 5:405)), Kidera (Kidera factors (J Protein Chem 4:23)), Miyazawa (Miyazawa, contact energy from 3D structures (1985)), Parker (Parker, HYDROPHILICITY from HPLC retention (1986)), Ponnuswamy (Ponnuswamy, folded-protein character (Prog Biophys Mol Biol 59:57)), Rose (Rose (1985)), Roseman (Roseman (1988)), Sweet (Sweet, optimized matching OMH (1983)), Tanford (Tanford (1962)), Wilson (Wilson, hydrophobic constants from HPLC retention (1981)), Zimmerman (Zimmerman (J Theor Biol 21:170)). Only applies when kind is hydropathy.

scaleId.description: any of the 57 ExPASy ProtScale scales, or the 14 Biopython tables ProtScale does not publish. Pass this INSTEAD of `kind` and `scale`, never alongside them: sending `scaleId` together with `kind` is refused by name rather than one silently winning. The panel opens on `scaleId: hydropath-doolittle`, which computes the same curve as the `kind`/`scale` defaults. Values: molecularweight (Molecular weight), numbercodons (Number of codon(s)), bulkiness (Bulkiness), polarityzimmerman (Polarity / Zimmerman), polaritygrantham (Polarity / Grantham), refractivity (Refractivity), recognitionfactors (Recognition factors), hphob-eisenberg (Hphob. / Eisenberg et al.), hphob-sweet (Hphob. OMH / Sweet et al.), hphob-woods (Hphob. / Hopp & Woods), hydropath-doolittle (Hydropath. / Kyte & Doolittle), hphob-manavalan (Hphob. / Manavalan et al.), hphob-leo (Hphob. / Abraham & Leo), hphob-black (Hphob. / Black), hphob-breese (Hphob. / Bull & Breese), hphob-fauchere (Hphob. / Fauchere et al.), hphob-guy (Hphob. / Guy), hphob-janin (Hphob. / Janin), hphob-miyazawa (Hphob. / Miyazawa et al.), hphob-argos (Hphob. / Rao & Argos), hphob-roseman (Hphob. / Roseman), hphob-tanford (Hphob. / Tanford), hphob-wolfenden (Hphob. / Wolfenden et al.), hphob-welling (Hphob. / Welling & al), hphob-wilson (Hphob. HPLC / Wilson & al), hphob-parker (Hphob. HPLC / Parker & al), hphob-ph3-4 (Hphob. HPLC pH3.4 / Cowan), hphob-ph7-5 (Hphob. HPLC pH7.5 / Cowan), hphob-mobility (Hphob. / Rf mobility), hplchfba (HPLC / HFBA retention), hplctfa (HPLC / TFA retention), transmembranetendency (Transmembrane tendency), hplc2-1 (HPLC / retention pH 2.1), hplc7-4 (HPLC / retention pH 7.4), buriedresidues (% buried residues), accessibleresidues (% accessible residues), hphob-chothia (Hphob. / Chothia), hphob-rose (Hphob. / Rose & al), ratioside (Ratio hetero end/side), averageburied (Average area buried), averageflexibility (Average flexibility), alpha-helixfasman (alpha-helix / Chou & Fasman), beta-sheetfasman (beta-sheet / Chou & Fasman), beta-turnfasman (beta-turn / Chou & Fasman), alpha-helixroux (alpha-helix / Deleage & Roux), beta-sheetroux (beta-sheet / Deleage & Roux), beta-turnroux (beta-turn / Deleage & Roux), coilroux (Coil / Deleage & Roux), alpha-helixlevitt (alpha-helix / Levitt), beta-sheetlevitt (beta-sheet / Levitt), beta-turnlevitt (beta-turn / Levitt), totalbeta-strand (Total beta-strand), antiparallelbeta-strand (Antiparallel beta-strand), parallelbeta-strand (Parallel beta-strand), a-a-composition (A.A. composition), a-a-swiss-prot (A.A. comp. in Swiss-Prot), relativemutability (Relative mutability), biopython-argos (Argos), biopython-casari (Casari & Sippl), biopython-cid (Cid et al.), biopython-engelman (Engelman (GES)), biopython-fasman (Fasman), biopython-goldsack (Gold Sack & Chalifoux), biopython-jones (Jones), biopython-juretic (Juretic et al.), biopython-kidera (Kidera et al.), biopython-ponnuswamy (Ponnuswamy), biopython-zimmerman (Zimmerman (hydrophobicity)), biopython-flex (Flexibility (Vihinen)), biopython-surface-accessibility (Surface accessibility (Emini)), biopython-janin (Janin (Biopython rounding)).

weightVariation.description: ProtScale's weight model between the centre and the edge weight: 'linear' steps down evenly, 'exponential' decays steeply near the centre. Requires `scaleId`; identical at edge 1.

window.description: ProtScale window in residues, odd (default 9). IGNORED for 'flexibility', whose Vihinen parameters are only defined at 9. Only applies when kind is hydropathy or hydrophilicity or accessibility or interior.

name: protein_profile

centres.description: 0-based residue index each window centres on, parallel to `values`

normalized.description: whether the scale was rescaled to 0-1 before windowing. False for the five ProtParam kinds, which are never rescaled

peak.description: index into `values` of the LARGEST value. Large is not a synonym for hydrophobic: on a transfer free energy or a hydrophilicity scale the largest window is the most hydrophilic one, and on a flexibility or accessibility profile it is neither. `label` names the scale; `protein_properties.gravyHydrophobicEnd` answers the direction for the 28 hydropathy tables

peakResidue.description: 1-based residue the peak window centres on

plot.description: the profile as a plot along the chain

reference.description: the scale's primary citation, when it came from the ProtScale catalogue. Empty for the five ProtParam kinds

trough.description: index into `values` of the SMALLEST value — the other extreme, which is the hydrophobic one on an inverted scale

troughResidue.description: 1-based residue the trough window centres on

weightVariation.description: the ProtScale weight model the values were computed under, 'linear' or 'exponential' ('linear' for the five ProtParam kinds)
